name: The Charmels
hook: A Stax girl group with no national hit, whose sad piano intro became the sound of Wu-Tang's 'C.R.E.A.M.'.
blurb: The Charmels were a girl group on Volt, part of the Stax label in Memphis. They made a handful of singles, and none became a national hit; their end year is approximate. 'As Long as I've Got You' (1967) was written by Isaac Hayes and David Porter, the Stax songwriting team behind 'Soul Man'. In 1993 RZA sampled its piano for the Wu-Tang Clan's 'C.R.E.A.M.', and a record almost nobody knew became the sound of one of rap's most famous songs. It is the clearest case on the map of sampling as rediscovery: an obscure single made famous a generation later by a producer digging for a mood rather than for drums.
